messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: stan::agrad::var for boost math
parts:
I finally found the doc I was looking for, which outlines
what you need to do to integrate a new scalar type into
Boost:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_48_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/using_udt/concepts.html

We should be good to go, because stan::agrad::var is
defined for all the built-in arithmetic operations and
assignments and because I just defined std::numerics<stan::agrad::var>,
everything else can be derived by template metaprogramming
according to footnotes 1-3 on the above page.

Here's a nice example of bindings for arbitrary
precision real arithmetic:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_48_0/boost/math/bindings/rr.hpp

Given that the default implementations of std::numeric_limits<T>
for non-primitive type T just threw exceptions for all the
constants, I don't think they'll get created willy nilly, because
we haven't seen any such exceptions.

Good templated code will use the std::numeric_limits<T> template
for constants.

There's also a nice example of how to do more general comparison
operations. I'll retrofit these onto our auto-dif, which should
make them more flexible. (It's exactly problems like this at
an even more basic level that prohibited our use of the other
auto-dif libs -- all sorts of basic ops were missing or ill-defined
to return constants rather than refs or things like that.)

- Bob
